  Terse gloss: "Aramaic preposition: upon, over, on; to, unto; concerning, about; against; because of; more than"
  Readable gloss: "An Aramaic preposition found exclusively in the bilingual sections of Ezra and Daniel, functioning as the counterpart to Hebrew 'al. Its spatial core means 'upon' or 'over,' but context stretches it across a wide range: direction ('to, unto'), topic ('concerning'), opposition ('against'), cause ('because of'), and even comparison ('more than'). Nebuchadnezzar's fury burned 'against' the three youths (Dan 3:19), while the same form in the same verse expresses degree — his face changed 'more than' was fitting. Tracing its suffixed forms across the Aramaic chapters reveals how a single preposition anchors an entire web of relational meanings."

  Sense 1: "upon, on, over"
    Enriched: The primary spatial-superessive sense — 'upon, on, over' — accounting for 75 of 103 occurrences. This covers physical position on a surface, authority exercised over a domain, and general superposition. Spanish sobre, French sur, and German ueber all converge on this core spatial meaning, appearing consistently throughout the Aramaic sections of Ezra and Daniel (Ezra 4:11-20; Dan 2:28-46).
    Existing Spanish translations: a, en, sobre, sobre-
  Sense 2: "to, unto"
    Enriched: A directional or dative extension meaning 'to, unto' — indicating movement toward or the indirect recipient of an action. Thirteen occurrences carry this sense, as in letters sent 'to' the king (Ezra 4:11-12; 5:7). French sur and German ueber remain unchanged, but Spanish shifts to the directional a, revealing the semantic extension from position to goal.
    Existing Spanish translations: a, a-, a-mí, a-nosotros, a-nosotros., a-él, ante, y-a
  Sense 3: "concerning, about"
    Enriched: A topical or referential sense meaning 'concerning, about, regarding' — the preposition marks the subject under discussion. Daniel's companions declare they need not answer the king 'concerning' the matter (Dan 3:16); Daniel is praised for wisdom found 'in' him 'concerning' interpretation (Dan 5:14). Eight occurrences carry this discourse-framing function.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-sobre-, [de-ti], sobre, sobre-
  Sense 4: "against"
    Enriched: An adversative sense meaning 'against' — expressing opposition or hostility. Rehum and Shimshai write 'against' Jerusalem (Ezra 4:8); Nebuchadnezzar's expression changes 'against' Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego (Dan 3:19). Four occurrences, consistently rendered by Spanish contra, distinguishing this from the neutral spatial sense.
    Existing Spanish translations: contra, contra-
  Sense 5: "because of, on account of"
    Enriched: A causal sense meaning 'because of, on account of' — indicating reason or grounds for an action. Daniel asks Arioch 'why' (literally 'on account of what') the decree is so harsh (Dan 2:15), and the vision was given not 'because of' Daniel's own wisdom but for the king's sake (Dan 2:30). Only two clear occurrences, both in Daniel 2.
    Existing Spanish translations: para, ¿por-qué
  Sense 6: "more than, beyond"
    Enriched: A comparative-superlative sense meaning 'more than, beyond' — a single occurrence in Daniel 3:19 where Nebuchadnezzar orders the furnace heated seven times 'more than' was customary. Spanish mas de explicitly marks the comparative, while the other languages use their standard rendering, showing how context alone disambiguates this rare extension.
    Existing Spanish translations: más-de
